about: Round 4's routing table, pre-registered data. Decided by routing.py only, from harness-side records only, never from the agent's text. Route, phase, turn-end and batch-state strings are graders/labels4.py's and are checked against it on load. A row matches when the take is in its phase, every all_of condition holds, at least one any_of condition holds (when any_of is given), and no none_of condition holds. The winning rows are the matched rows at the highest precedence level; matched rows at that level that name different routes are a tie and are refused, as is an input that matches no row. Rows never read a text-derived count (the events record): those are annotations, below.

It raises RoutingRefused, so batch records the take blocked, and it ranks above pause.' In every phase (when any) and outranked by nothing (W4BR-w4h-7): an API error of the take whose status, type or text carries a spend-cap marker of the take's own harness (spend_cap_markers, read by the take's pin.harness; text by round 3's bounded search, word-bounded and case-insensitive; the harness-side error fields only, never the agent's reply) is refused for a human ruling, whatever else matches, so a spend-cap 429 never reaches the rate-limit row: it never re-runs and never waits for a usage window. No route is added to labels4.ROUTES. routing.py checks the rule: its keys, its phase, an empty outranked_by, and conditions that read only the API-error fields with in_spend_cap_markers; and that no spend-cap marker of a harness is also one of its rate-limit markers.

transcript-mismatch.ruling: the lane orchestrator's approval of fold plan prefreeze-1, Sat 24 Oct 2026, under Javier's standing delegation (pre-freeze review 1, MAJOR 7): the session file a claude-code take is graded from, and a Codex or Gemini take's native store, sit on the take's read-write config mount owned by the agent's uid, and the cross-checks bound ids, so one in-take command that rewrote a reply's words passed. The checker compares the content of each turn with the host-captured stream (claude-code: every main-thread text, thinking, tool_use and tool_result, in order; codex: each command's argv; gemini: each tool result's output), from the committed records alone. A difference is something the agent can cause, so by the plan's rule for graded (no try is ever discarded or re-run for something the agent did) it is never re-run: it routes by its own row, transcript-mismatch, aborted after the agent's first turn (published, counted against holding, never re-run), outranking the generic operator-reason row, except beside harness-condition-violated, which keeps glitch-b5's ruling 3 (harness-error); before the first turn it routes a rehearsal by the generic row. tests/test_routing.py TestRound4Additions and tests/test_pf1_transcript_integrity.py bind it.
transcript-mismatch.meaning: the take's graded record and its host-captured turn streams disagree in content: a claude-code turn's text, thinking, tool calls or tool results in the session file are not its stream's, in order; a Codex exec stream's command, split as a shell line, is not the rollout's argv for it; or a Gemini stream's tool result output is not the native session's display of that call; and (the lane orchestrator's ruling on review fb354328, 24 Oct 2026: after the first turn nothing only the agent-writable records show routes harness-error or rehearsal) the session file carries an auto_mode attachment or a deferred_tools_delta adding a denied tool, an operator line that is not its launch journal's prompt, a line that is not one JSON record, a line separator or a sidechain record no turn stream carries, or a native store does not read while every host stream reads whole

The config folder's session store must hold only the take's own session after every turn and at publish, every turn's sweep of the take container must find no session but the take's own, and no Bash command line may carry the --no-session-persistence switch (by its prefix) or assign or export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME, GEMINI_CLI_HOME or HOME in assignment position; otherwise the take fails closed (reviews r14 and r15, the same day). It routes by the generic operator-reason rows like harness-condition-violated: harness-error after the agent's first turn, a rehearsal before it. tests/test_routing.py TestRound4Additions binds it.

harness-condition-violated.ruling: glitch-6b's ruling, 15 Oct 2026, under Javier's delegation (Javier approved the bash-first steer off, "Your call sounds good"): every claude-code take runs with CLAUDE_CODE_THRIFTY_SONIC off, and (the isolation ruling, the same day) denies RemoteTrigger, SendMessage and ListAgents; a take where such a harness condition failed is routed as harness-error, since a harness condition failed, which is not the agent's behaviour. It routes by the generic operator-reason rows, harness-error after the agent's first turn (a rehearsal before it, as every operator reason). glitch-b5's ruling 3 (17 Oct 2026, under Javier's delegation): a take that violates the harness's own study conditions is a harness fault, not a model outcome; it is never graded as the model's result, it is voided with its reason recorded and its cell is re-run (harness-error after the first turn, under that route's cap; a rehearsal before it), and until routed it fails closed. So it outranks the cgroup counters: cgroup-kill's none_of names it, and beside a cgroup kill it routes harness-error, never aborted. tests/test_routing.py TestRound4Additions and TestHarnessConditionVoided bind it.
harness-condition-violated.meaning: a study harness condition did not hold for the take, fail closed on every turn (glitch-6b, 15 Oct 2026): a turn has no launch journal, or its journal does not set CLAUDE_CODE_THRIFTY_SONIC to "false", deny RemoteTrigger, SendMessage and ListAgents (--disallowedTools and permissions.deny) or set crossSessionInbound "refuse"; or a turn's stream init still offers a denied isolation tool. Since the lane orchestrator's ruling on review fb354328 (24 Oct 2026) it reads host records alone: an auto_mode attachment or a deferred_tools_delta that only the agent-writable transcript shows is transcript-mismatch

rehearsal.source: Key renamed from reruns_per_half_cell (glitch-f3, 6 Oct 2026): the value counts the half-cell's committed rehearsals, this one included, so it allows at most cap−1 re-runs. Round 3's prereg.json sets rehearsal_cap = 3 (at e2979b3143081824aadea73523ec41af30c1ddb1), and takes.py:286-291 there applies it per cell (task, half, model): a cell that has had rehearsal_cap rehearsals registers no further attempt: 'It publishes `incomplete — mechanical` with each reason, and no further attempt is registered.' Unit (glitch-f3's ruling, in-plan, 6 Oct 2026; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's): the cap counts the rehearsals committed in the half-cell, round 3's unit, round 3's cell (task, half, model) being round 4's half-cell (arm, task, half, model), the registered row's half_cell, with wording and repeat or pressure as the slot inside it. batch.py counts every committed rehearsal of the half-cell, one by one (a take a ruling routes rehearsal counts too: review round 3, W1B3-1); the one that brings the count to the cap is its slot's last (never re-run) and is committed with the cell state labels4.INCOMPLETE_MECHANICAL and its reason; nothing more is registered for that half-cell, and the loop goes on with the other half-cells. Each rehearsal's own reasons stay in its own committed record.

pause.source: Key renamed from reruns_per_half_cell (glitch-f3, 6 Oct 2026): the value counts the half-cell's usage-window events of pause, the one that reaches it included, so at most cap−1 of them are re-run (W1B3-5, below). Plan: 're-run in the same slot under round 3's pause_cap'. Round 3's files say two things, both recorded here (review round 2, W1B2-11). Its driver, evals/gap-study-3/drive.py:147-148 at e2979b3143081824aadea73523ec41af30c1ddb1 (review 13, F6): 'a pause is uncapped where a rehearsal is capped, so a death before the first turn whose message merely says "resets" must not be read as a pause.' Its pre-registration nonetheless sets pause_cap = 3 (evals/gap-study-3/prereg.json), and evals/gap-study-3/takes.py:280-285 applies it per cell (task, half, model): 'A pause frees a slot on the driver's record alone, so it is capped like a rehearsal; the cell publishes `incomplete — mechanical` and no further attempt is registered.' The pre-registered value is the one round 3 enforced (takes.py reads pre['pause_cap']), and round 4 copies it, 3 per half-cell, under Javier's ruling "gap4 routing: A" (6 Oct 2026). Unit (glitch-f3's ruling, in-plan, 6 Oct 2026; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's): the cap counts per half-cell, round 3's unit, round 3's cell (task, half, model) being round 4's half-cell (arm, task, half, model), the registered row's half_cell, with wording and repeat or pressure as the slot inside it. What it counts (glitch-f3's ruling on review round 3, W1B3-5, in-plan, 6 Oct 2026, relayed by the gap4 lane lead; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's): the half-cell's usage-window events, so the pauses that share one reset count once. The cap bounds window events, round 3's own unit: round 3 drove one take at a time, so each of its pauses was its own window event, while round 4 drives up to three takes at once in a rolling window (lane vendor-b19, glitch-26's rulings B19-5 and B19-7, 19 Oct 2026) and every pause committed between two of the loop's waits for the usage window shares the one reset the second wait is for (at most three pauses, one per slot: the drives in flight when the first was seen). Each committed pause carries its window_event, and batch.py counts the distinct window events among the half-cell's committed pauses (a take a ruling routes pause counts as its own event: review round 3, W1B3-1); the take whose window event brings the count to the cap is its slot's last (never re-run) and is committed with the cell state labels4.INCOMPLETE_MECHANICAL and its reason, as is every later take of that half-cell; nothing more is registered for it, and the loop goes on with the other half-cells (still waiting for the usage window before its next launch).

pin_refusal.source: Review round 3, W1B3-2: the gap4 lane lead's ruling, whose stricter reading glitch-f3 accepted (in-plan, 6 Oct 2026, relayed by the gap4 lane lead; recorded as glitch-f3's, not the owner's), carrying glitch-f3's fold-3 ruling 2, 'a differing init is refused for a human, a pin mismatch'. Before the agent's first turn, a take whose init events include one that is present and differs from the pin (its model, mode or version) is refused for a human, whatever else matches: no before-first-turn harness row (an API error, no-first-agent-turn, a container exit, a silent timeout) turns a pin mismatch into a rehearsal. Only a route in outranked_by wins over it, the rate-limit pause, because pause outranks every route and a usage limit is not a pin fault. A missing init event never triggers it (glitch-f3's fold-3 ruling: a CLI that never printed its init event is harness-side). After the first turn the init-mismatch row routes a differing or missing init as harness-error, as the plan says. Its scope is this one rule, on its all_of line: if glitch-f3 narrows it to timed-out ends only, that is one condition appended there, {"path": "ledger.end", "op": "eq", "value": "timed-out"}. routing.py checks the rule: before the first turn, conditions on harness records only, and only routes that outrank rehearsal may outrank it.

agent_event_rows.source: Pre-freeze review 2, MAJOR 1 (fold plan prefreeze-2, MAJOR 1 (glitch-45, the lane orchestrator, 29 Oct 2026, under Javier's standing delegation; the orchestrator's, not the owner's), lane L-A1) adds store-variable-assigned, the row of agent_event_reasons' one id. Pre-freeze review 1, MAJOR 5, folded by lane pf1-l2a under the Lane-orchestrator's approval of the fold plan (Sat 24 Oct 2026, under Javier's standing delegation; the orchestrator's, not the owner's, reported to him after): the graded after-first-turn rows whose records the agent itself can produce, a non-zero exit of its own CLI and a process of its own alive at the quiescence cap. Each id is an event of the take it routes: when one is among a graded take's winning rows, run.py's record_for writes it into the record's agent_events (in this order), and stats counts each in its own column of the agent-caused routes table, beside the take's ordinary reading. routing.py checks that every id is a row of this table, phase after-first-turn, route graded. The watcher's queue overflow (inotify's, the sidecar's queue_overflow) is not one: it routes harness-error by watcher-gap, because a watcher that lost events leaves an end state that cannot be read whole, so a take whose agent provoked the overflow stays harness-error, never graded on a partial record, and that road is owed a line in the draft's box_residuals (the fold plan's MAJOR 5, written with the draft's texts).

agent_reach.source: fold plan prefreeze-2, MAJOR 1, step 1 (glitch-45, the lane orchestrator, 29 Oct 2026, under Javier's standing delegation; the orchestrator's, not the owner's), lane L-A1 (pre-freeze review 2, MAJOR 1: the agent's own ordinary commands routed its take to harness-error, where it was re-run and a forbidden change it made was in no view; round 1's MAJOR 5 and round 2's MAJOR 1 each found instances, so the class is folded, not the instance). The question, for every row that does not route graded after the agent's first turn (row:), the two rules above the rows (rule:) and every checker reason routing reads (reason:): can the agent produce the record this reads, and how (answered from code, file and function named)? route is the route the table then gives (a reason's: a clean after-first-turn take carrying it alone; refused for a refusal). The rule the fold applies: an agent-reachable route is aborted or graded, never re-run or refused, unless call states a named exception with its reason or a ruling owed; every harness-error attempt's end state is now read for a forbidden change (run.STOPPED_ROUTES). routing.check_table refuses a missing or extra entry, a stated route that is not the table's, and a reachable re-running or refusing entry with no call. tests/test_pf2_class_table.py binds it.

annotations_about: Annotations are decided on every take, in every phase, whatever route wins and even when routing refuses the take: they never route. An annotation holds when at least one of its any_of conditions holds; it is reported as an event when event is true, and sets mask (the take's text is masked, never deleted, before commit) when mask is true.
